In the middle-income countries there are two major
types of health systems, distinguished by whether
the government or the private sector provides
health insurance. Health spending, at $20 to $400
per capita, is higher than in low-income countries,
and both public and private managerial capacity is
stronger. In countries with private insurance, such
as South Africa and Zimbabwe, the government
uses general revenues to pay for health care for
middle- and low-income groups, while upper-
income households (less than 20 percent of the
